title: Vertical Stabiliser Fin Box Rib Crack Repair by Doubler and Angle
abstract: Permanent repair of a crack in a fin box rib web by a doubler and angle combination, with the access route through the fin leading edge and the torsion box entry precautions.

sections.purpose: Permanent repair of a crack in the web of a fin box rib, using a doubler on the web with an angle at the rib to spar joint, carried out from inside the torsion box.
sections.damage_assessment: Cracks in the fin box rib web are rare and are usually found during a scheduled internal inspection rather than as a result of a reported event. The assessment must establish whether the crack has reached the rib to spar joint fastener row; a crack in the joint row changes the load path into the spar and is outside this scheme. Access is from inside the torsion box and confined space entry precautions apply, which limits the working time per shift and must be planned for. The rib web thickness must be measured at four positions, because the doubler is sized against the local thickness and the web is tapered.
sections.repair_procedure: Open the fin leading edge access and prepare the torsion box for entry, observing the confined space precautions. Remove the protective treatment in the repair area. Establish the crack extent by eddy current and stop-drill both crack tips. Measure the web thickness at the four positions given on repair drawing RD-55-30-11-008. Prepare the doubler landing area on the web. Position the doubler using the plate D5530110749890 and install the angle D5530119137814 at the rib to spar joint as shown. Drill the fastener pattern through doubler and web, taking care not to break into the joint fastener row. Install the fasteners AES932279K1 wet. Fit the closing item SAD726961-22 at the upper edge of the doubler. Restore the protective treatment over the whole repair area and confirm no tooling or debris is left in the torsion box before the access is closed.
sections.inspection_requirements: Eddy current inspection of the stop-drilled holes and the doubler fastener rows after installation. A repeat eddy current inspection is required every 12 000 flight hours, which aligns with the scheduled internal fin inspection so that no additional access is needed. Photographic record of the repair is required, because the next inspection will be done by a different team and the repair is not easy to locate from the access opening.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Cracks up to 35 mm in the rib web, not reaching the rib to spar joint fastener row and not within 20 mm of a lightening hole edge.

repair_drawings.title: Web doubler and joint angle, fin box rib

type_data.fastener_pattern: Two rows of sixteen, 20 mm pitch, 14 mm edge distance, clear of the joint fastener row by at least 25 mm
type_data.fatigue_life_note: Not life limited. Repeat eddy current inspection every 12 000 flight hours, aligned with the scheduled internal fin inspection.
